userStories.title: Host: broadcast `node-patched` diffs to all peers after successful apply
userStories.description: As all connected peers, we need the host to emit a `node-patched` frame after every accepted edit so every peer converges to the same state — including the originator (so optimistic state is reconciled against the canonical write).

Extend apps/studio/src/share.ts `handleRpcFrame` so after a successful op (`outcome.kind === 'ok'`), the controller calls `this.broadcast({ v: 1, type: 'node-patched', from: 'host', to: 'all', payload: { flowId, op, diff, version } })` BEFORE returning the `rpc-result` — order matters: peers should already see the patch when their `rpc-result` arrives so the originator's optimistic reconcile is a no-op

Add a per-flow version counter `Map<flowId, number>` on the ShareController instance; bump before broadcasting; include in the payload (peers use this only for tie-breaking out-of-order frames in a future story — for now just monotonic-increasing assertion in tests)

Diff shape: for moveNode → `{ kind: 'move', nodeId, position }`; for patchNode → `{ kind: 'patch', nodeId, patch: <body minus flowId> }`; for addNode → `{ kind: 'add', node: <full new node> }`; for deleteNode → `{ kind: 'delete', nodeId }`; for reorderNode → `{ kind: 'reorder', nodeId, op: <ReorderOp> }`; connector variants follow the same kind pattern with `connectorId` instead of `nodeId`

userStories.title: Peer: optimistic apply with revert-on-reject in share-client
userStories.description: As a peer, I want my edits to feel instant — applied to my local canvas state immediately and reverted only if the host returns `{ ok: false }` — so the canvas matches the design doc's optimistic UX without flicker on the happy path.
acceptanceCriteria: Working dir: /Users/tuongaz/dev/seeflow-viewer

Extend src/lib/share-client.ts with an `OptimisticStore` class (or hook factory if functional fits better) that holds the last-known-good flow snapshot keyed by `flowId` and a per-RPC-id stack of inverse patches (so reverts apply in LIFO order on multi-pending failure)

When `createIoAdapter`'s methods send an `rpc` frame, the wrapper FIRST applies the optimistic change locally — e.g. `moveNode` writes the new position into the in-memory flow snapshot, pushes the inverse `{ op: 'moveNode', nodeId, position: previousPosition }` onto the revert stack keyed by the same `id`
On `rpc-result { ok: true }`: discard the revert entry (host's `node-patched` broadcast — handled in US-042 — is the canonical state)
On `rpc-result { ok: false, reason }`: apply the inverse patch, surface a toast event via `client.emit('edit-reverted', { reason, op })` so the SPA's toast layer can display "Edit reverted: <reason>"
On timeout / disconnect (US-040 failure paths), treat the same as `ok: false` — revert + toast `"Disconnected from host"`

userStories.description: As Phase 4's exit criterion, I need an integration test that boots the host studio + relay (or a stub) + two simulated peer clients and asserts that a moveNode from peer A is observed by peer B within ~100 ms with the host's flow.json updated on disk.
